A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
supported_en: Netherlands Cancer Registry study (Annals of Oncology 2012): 7 points fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became available.
not_supported_en: No page shows the 8% share of elderly stage I patients we assume, or any Finnish data on untreated stage I patients.
in_use_quote: Jos kyseessä on pieni keuhkotuumori eikä kasvain ole paikallisesti edennyt, voidaan antaa täsmäsädehoitoa mikäli potilaan yleistila tai muut sairaudet eivät salli operatiivista hoitoa.
missing_en: No page says that every inoperable stage I patient must be referred for stereotactic radiotherapy, or that Hyvaks has such a rule.
summary_en: The KYS lung cancer care pathway (published 2021) says that precision radiotherapy ("täsmäsädehoito") can be given for a small, localised tumour when the patient's condition rules out surgery. It also says that every lung cancer patient is discussed at least once in a meeting where the treatment decision is made. The Central Finland (Hyvaks) patient pathway lists radiotherapy as an option but does not mention stereotactic treatment or a referral rule. A Dutch national registry study (Annals of Oncology, 2012) found 7 percentage points fewer untreated elderly stage I patients once stereotactic radiotherapy was fully available, which fits the model's assumption.
unanswered_en: No page shows whether stereotactic radiotherapy is given at Sairaala Nova, or how many stage I patients in Central Finland go untreated.
